newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda says global coffee limits not conclusive.
newsitem.headline: Uganda says global coffee limits not conclusive.

text.p: Ugandan coffee authorities said on Friday that last month's meeting of producers in Brazil on export limits was "not conclusive" and the matter would be discussed at another forum in the near future.

A senior official of the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said "the question of limitations on quantity put on the market is something that is still being discussed, people are trying to see whether quantity can be reduced".
At the Brazil meeting last month, the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) agreed to cut members' coffee exports by 1.3 million 60-kg bags between January and June 1997.
Traders said the producers aimed to reduce coffee supply on the market from a forecast 53 million bags to 52 million in 1996/97.
African robusta coffee producers early in February said they would undertake the export cuts outlined by the ACPC.
But on Wednesday, another UCDA official said Uganda was unlikely to retain 1996/97 exports in line with the Brazil undertaking because drought and disease meant exports would be reduced anyway.

"But even if such quotas are allocated, they are likely to be superseded by current (declining) procurement," a senior official at the UCDA told Reuters in Kampala on Wednesday. "Uganda will not need to reduce exports to meet quotas."
On Friday, though, the senior UCDA official said: "There are no quotas, so we cannot speak of meeting our quota. The matter of limitations has been discussed and is still under discussion."
He added: "We do not want to send the wrong signals to the market. We do not want anyone to say we have reneged or are backing down on positions previously taken in negotiations."
The senior official did not say when or where the next producers' forum, when the sensitive matter of limitations would be discussed again, would be held.
But the Interafrican Coffee Organisation said last week that African coffee producers would meet in Abidjan on March 6-7 for talks on implementing the robusta export limit set in Brazil.
Ugandan industry officials have said capricious weather and disease will combine to cut Uganda's coffee exports in 1996/97 from a bumper level achieved in the previous season.

Ugandan authorities have already forecast exports in the range of 3.6 million to 3.8 million bags in 1996/97 but drought and a faster-than-expected spread of the disease meant the figure would be much lower than that, industry officials said.
Ugandan coffee exports in 1995/96 were around 4.1 million 60-kg bags compared to 2.8 million bags in 1994/95.
Traditionally, the bulk of Ugandan coffee is harvested in the first half of the coffee season (October to March), which coincides with peak consumption in the northern hemisphere.
UCDA officials forecast exports at 1,122,484 bags in the second quarter (January to March 1997), worth $90.37 million.

Uganda exported 1,290,986 bags of coffee worth $95.2 million in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October-December) from 795,502 bags worth $88.1 million in the same period last year. The first quarter volume was the highest quarterly figure realised in four years.
UCDA officials said the real impact of the poor weather and disease would be seen in a poor third quarter, while the fourth quarter would confirm the forecast of declining exports.
